sentences.text: The genus Acanthopleurus was described by Agassiz in 1844.

Acanthopleurus is classified in the kingdom Animalia, phylum Chordata, class Actinopterygii, order Tetraodontiformes, and family Xenacanthidae, though the Paleobiology Database classifies it in the class Chondrichthyes.
The genus contains three species: A. collettei, A. serratus, and A. trispinosus.
The former species A. brevis is now classified in the separate genus Cryptobalistes.
This animal lived in the seas over modern-day Europe during the early Oligocene epoch.
The species A. collettei and the type species A. serratus both inhabited the Oligocene of Switzerland within the Matt Formation.
The species A. trispinosus lived in the Oligocene of Romania.
